patterns.name: Case study with a sticky meta rail
patterns.mechanism: The left rail stays sticky and shows role, stack, year and outcome. The right column scrolls through Problem, Approach, Result, and Images. The page ends with next/previous project links.

patterns.name: Work index with a hover preview
patterns.mechanism: Projects are listed as full-width rows (title, discipline, year). On hover, a preview image follows the cursor with a spring (stiffness 300, damping 30). On touch, each row expands inline instead.

patterns.name: Answer-first FAQ (AEO)
patterns.mechanism: Each question is written the way a buyer would ask it, as an H3. The answer that follows opens with a direct 40–60 word reply before any detail. The whole block is sourced from content/faq/*.json and emitted as FAQPage JSON-LD.

patterns.name: Numbered services with outcomes
patterns.mechanism: Services are numbered (01, 02, 03) and each gets one outcome sentence and a 3-item deliverables list. Expanding one uses a layout animation. Each service links to its own page for SEO.

patterns.name: Inline short contact form
patterns.mechanism: Name, email and message only. It uses a server action with a Turnstile check. On success the page shows an inline confirmation instead of redirecting, and the direct email appears next to the form as an alternative.

patterns.name: Minimal top bar with a full-screen overlay menu
patterns.mechanism: The top bar holds only the logo, 3 or fewer links and a CTA. On mobile, the menu opens as a full-screen overlay with large type and staggered links. It traps focus and closes on Esc.

patterns.name: Footer with an oversized CTA
patterns.mechanism: The footer opens with a huge 'Let's talk' link to email or contact, followed by a sitemap in columns, socials, and a local time/location stamp.

patterns.name: Restrained scroll reveals
patterns.mechanism: Content reveals once, on entering the viewport: opacity 0→1 and y 16→0 over 500ms with ease [0.22,1,0.36,1]. Items stagger by 40ms. There are no parallax stacks. Under reduced motion content appears instantly. Never on content that can sit in the first viewport at any breakpoint: initial opacity 0 until hydration pushed starter mobile LCP from 2.46s to 3.9s (observed 2026-09-25, marketing-starter).

patterns.name: Scroll driven cinematic sequence
patterns.mechanism: Pre-render scene clips with frame-identical seams and map scroll progress to playback time. Keep the narrative and fallback readable without video.
good_for: media-led launch pages with a tested lightweight fallback

patterns.name: Tell the project as a sequence of decisions and proof
patterns.mechanism: Structure each project as situation → problem → system decision → real interaction → verified outcome → limit/source. Every crucial fact remains readable without animation or video. A film illustrates the sequence; its source and limits sit next to the claim.

sources.evidence: Owner clips 3debcee4 and 02528445 (0:03–0:19): sequential scenes and interactive storytelling; mechanism paraphrased, outcome untested.

patterns.name: Use an owner-chosen motif to connect chapters
patterns.mechanism: When the owner explicitly supplies a personal craft or experience as the story theme, translate one recognizable mechanism (e.g. a skate line or wheel marks) into navigation and chapter transitions. Keep the actual projects, claims and actions primary; ask for source proof before publishing biographical achievements.
bad_for: client marketing without explicit owner choice

sources.evidence: Clip 6baaa3d7 (0:03–0:16) presents a distinctive portfolio identity with an illustrated portrait and project gallery. Applying the mechanism to skating is owner-directed; no underlying asset is reused.

patterns.name: Make a real project film an explicit user action
patterns.mechanism: Offer separate case navigation and a labeled Play film action only after an actual source-backed clip is reviewed and available. Click-to-play with a poster, duration, native controls, captions/transcript and text summary; no autoplay audio. Do not treat promotional editing as benchmark evidence.
bad_for: claims supported only by edited promotional video

sources.evidence: Clip 6baaa3d7 shows projects as visual episodes; clip 02528445 shows interactive site storytelling. Video actions are an owner-requested portfolio feature; implementation and performance are not yet tested.
